sources.title: How are earthquakes detected, located and measured?

facts.statement: Deprem, yer kabuğunda biriken gerinim enerjisinin aniden serbest kalmasıdır.
facts.quote: An earthquake is the sudden release of strain energy in the Earth’s crust
facts.location: British Geological Survey — Earthquakes

facts.statement: Dünya'nın dört temel katmanı vardır: katı kabuk, sıcak ve neredeyse katı manto, sıvı dış çekirdek ve katı iç çekirdek.
facts.quote: a solid crust, a hot, nearly solid mantle, a liquid outer core and a solid inner core. / The earth has four major layers: the inner core, outer core, mantle and crust
facts.location: NASA Space Place — What Is an Earthquake?; USGS — The Science of Earthquakes

facts.statement: Dünya'nın en dış katmanı tektonik levha denen yaklaşık 15 büyük parçaya bölünmüştür; levhalar birbirine göre çok yavaş, tipik olarak yılda birkaç santimetre hareket eder.
facts.quote: The Earth’s outermost layer is fragmented into about 15 major slabs called tectonic plates. / Tectonic plates move very slowly relative to each other, typically a few centimetres per year
facts.location: British Geological Survey — What causes earthquakes?

facts.statement: Levhalar birbirine doğru hareket edebilir, birbirine sürtünerek kayabilir ya da birbirinden ayrılabilir.
facts.quote: Continental and oceanic plates may move toward each other, scrape past each other, or pull apart
facts.location: National Geographic Education — Earthquakes

facts.statement: Sürtünme kayaları yerinde tutar ve gerilim birikir; fayın iki yanındaki kayalar yavaş yavaş biçim değiştirir; blokları kaydıracak enerji depolanır.
facts.quote: Friction, however, holds the rocks in place, causing stresses to build. / Before an earthquake, the buildup of stress in the rocks on either side of a fault results in gradual deformation. / the energy that would normally cause the blocks to slide past one another is being stored up.
facts.location: National Geographic Education — Earthquakes; British Geological Survey — What causes earthquakes?; USGS — The Science of Earthquakes

facts.statement: Elastik geri sekme: kayalar özgün biçimine döner ama fayın iki yanında yer değiştirmiş olur.
facts.quote: return to their original shape (elastic rebound) but are offset on either side of the fault.
facts.location: British Geological Survey — What causes earthquakes?

facts.statement: Depremin başladığı noktaya odak ya da hiposantr denir ve kilometrelerce derinde olabilir; odağın tam üstündeki yüzey noktası merkez üssüdür.
facts.quote: The point where an earthquake starts is termed the focus or hypocentre and may be many kilometres deep within the earth. / The point at the surface directly above the focus is called the earthquake epicentre.
facts.location: British Geological Survey — Earthquakes

facts.statement: Enerji, gölcükteki halkalar gibi her yöne yayılır.
facts.quote: the energy spreads out in all directions like ripples on a pond.
facts.location: British Geological Survey — Earthquakes

facts.statement: P dalgaları ilerleme yönü boyunca sıkışma ve genleşmelerden oluşur; S dalgalarının hareketi ilerleme yönüne diktir; P dalgaları S dalgalarından hızlıdır. Tipik yer kabuğunda P 5–7 km/s, S 3–4 km/s hızla ilerler.
facts.quote: P-waves are longitudinal waves that consist of a series of compressions and dilations along the direction of travel. / S-waves are transverse waves, whose motion is perpendicular to the direction of travel. / P waves are also faster than S waves / VP 5–7 km/s in typical Earth’s crust / VS 3–4 km/s in typical Earth’s crust
facts.location: British Geological Survey — How are earthquakes detected, located and measured?; USGS — The Science of Earthquakes

facts.statement: P dalgaları şimşek, S dalgaları gök gürültüsü gibidir; P'nin S'den hızlı olması depremin nerede olduğunu bulmayı sağlar.
facts.quote: P waves are like the lightning, and S waves are like the thunder. / P waves are also faster than S waves, and this fact is what allows us to tell where an earthquake was.
facts.location: USGS — The Science of Earthquakes

facts.statement: Sismograf ya da sismometre, sismogramı oluşturan ölçüm aletidir.
facts.quote: A seismograph or seismometer is the measuring instrument that creates the seismogram.
facts.location: British Geological Survey — How are earthquakes detected, located and measured?

facts.statement: Büyüklük ölçekleri logaritmiktir: büyüklükte bir birimlik artış, genlikte on katlık artışa karşılık gelir.
facts.quote: Earthquake magnitude scales are logarithmic, i.e. a one unit increase in magnitude corresponds to a tenfold increase in amplitude.
facts.location: British Geological Survey — How are earthquakes detected, located and measured?

facts.statement: Şiddet, depremin yol açtığı sarsıntının gücünün nitel ölçüsüdür ve normalde merkez üssünden uzaklaştıkça azalır; büyüklük ise uzaklıktan bağımsızdır.
facts.quote: Intensity is a qualitative measure of the strength of shaking caused by an earthquake / normally decreases with distance from the epicentre / is independent of distance from the epicentre.
facts.location: British Geological Survey — How are earthquakes detected, located and measured?

facts.statement: Dünya'da her gün yüzlerce deprem olur; ciddi hasar verebilecek büyüklükte olanlar yılda yaklaşık 100 tanedir.
facts.quote: Hundreds of earthquakes occur on Earth everyday. / There are around 100 earthquakes each year of a size that could cause serious damage.
facts.location: National Geographic Education — Earthquakes; British Geological Survey — Earthquakes

facts.statement: Artçı sarsıntılar ana depremden sonra haftalarca, aylarca, hatta yıllarca sürebilir.
facts.quote: aftershocks can continue for weeks, months, and even years after the mainshock!
facts.location: USGS — The Science of Earthquakes

facts.statement: Ne USGS ne de başka bilim insanları bugüne kadar büyük bir depremi önceden bildi; bir tahminin tarih ve saati, yeri ve büyüklüğü belirtmesi gerekir. Bilim insanları belirli bir fayda gelecekte yeniden deprem olacağını bilir.
facts.quote: Neither the USGS nor any other scientists have ever predicted a major earthquake. / 1) the date and time, 2) the location, and 3) the magnitude. / On any particular fault, scientists know there will be another earthquake sometime in the future
facts.location: USGS — Can you predict earthquakes?; USGS — The Science of Earthquakes

facts.statement: Erken uyarı, deprem başladıktan sonra yapılan bir bildirimdir.
facts.quote: Early warning is a notification that is issued after an earthquake starts.
facts.location: USGS — Can you predict earthquakes?

facts.statement: Deprem anında: yere çök, sağlam bir masanın altına gir, sarsıntı bitene kadar tutun; camlardan ve devrilebilecek eşyalardan uzak dur; dışarıdaysan binalardan, sokak lambalarından ve tellerden uzaklaş.
facts.quote: DROP to the ground. / Take COVER under a sturdy table or other heavy furniture. / HOLD ON until the shaking stops. / STAY AWAY from windows, glass, lighting fixtures, or furniture that could fall, like bookcases. / Move away from buildings, streetlights, and wires.
facts.location: Ready.gov Kids — Earthquakes

facts.statement: Hızla tahliye gerekirse ihtiyaç duyulacak eşyalarla bir acil durum çantası hazırlanmalıdır.
facts.quote: Build an emergency kit with items that you will need if you have to evacuate quickly.
facts.location: Ready.gov Kids — Earthquakes

facts.statement: Büyüklüğü 10 ya da daha fazla olan depremler olamaz.
facts.quote: No, earthquakes of magnitude 10 or larger cannot happen.
facts.location: USGS — Can you predict earthquakes?
